title: design-qa report (schemaVersion 2.0)
description: Agent-readable design-to-code parity report, schemaVersion 2.0 (breaking: only "2.0" validates). The design (a Figma file, a Figma prototype or a coded prototype, see meta.source) is the source of truth; findings are fixed in code, signed off as INTENTIONAL, explained as DATA or DISMISSED with a reason. Keys whose value may be null can be omitted (treated as null). Cross-field rules that JSON Schema cannot express (unique finding ids, findingIds/relatedFindings references, triage coverage, dismissal reasons, a signoff or knownDrift for INTENTIONAL, meta.figma for Figma sources, meta.screens consistency, pins on open FIX_CODE findings, crops inside the captured image, grounding in the capture on a remote target, full-length comparisons, derived scorecard values, pixel-diff bands against configured tolerances, the design-backfill rules) are enforced by scripts/validate.mjs. The optional backfill block (design backfill, step 2) sits beside the parity pass and never changes it. Properties marked "x-removed" name 1.x values with the message shown when they are used.

schemaVersion.errorMessage: schemaVersion 2.0 required; 1.x reports: re-run the pass

differences.description: Per state the worklist compared (build-report.mjs writes it; validate.mjs checks it against a rebuild): differing = the worklist's share of the page that differs (percent); regions = its regions that a finding or rejection names (key, percent, findings = finding ids, rejected = the reason, supported = a computed hint backs that reason); unlisted = regions beyond the worklist's caps that nothing names. Match and the verdict are derived from it.

rejections.description: What the agent looked at and decided not to report (build-report.mjs writes it from findings.json rejected[]): worklist regions, design-system audit candidates and compare rows, each with a reason. Shown in report.html and the fix plan; a rejected worklist share of a state's page above tolerances.pixelDiff.review holds the verdict at REVIEW.

key.description: The worklist item key, the audit candidate key, or for a compare row "<kind>:<state>:<elementClass | role \"name\" | selector>[:<property>]".

x-removed.SYNC_FIGMA: SYNC_FIGMA was removed in 2.0: reclassify as FIX_CODE or dismiss it

x-removed.MISSING_IN_DESIGN: MISSING_IN_DESIGN was removed in 2.0: the state matrix lists only states the design defines; drop this row

runId.description: Optional: the run id of the pass that built the report (the run lock <dir>/.design-qa-run.json, scripts/run.mjs). build-report.mjs writes it and refuses to rebuild a report of another run.

x-removed.sync: mode "sync" was removed in 2.0 (design → code only): use audit or fix

source.description: The source of truth the build is compared against.

tool.description: prototype sources only: what built the prototype

frame.description: viewport the design is compared at

figma.description: Required when meta.source.kind is figma or figma-prototype; frame must equal meta.source.frame when both exist.

screens.description: Multi-screen passes only. State ids are then written "<screen>/<state>" and every stateMatrix[].screen and findings[].screen is one of these ids.

variantOf.description: Optional: the meta.screens id this screen is a breakpoint variant of (e.g. "orders-600" with variantOf "orders" and its own frame size).

build.description: Written by build-report.mjs: the findings file and the evidence the report was built from, each with its sha256. validate.mjs and review.mjs verify them (verifyBuiltReport); a report without it is an evidence-gate error: write findings.json and build it.

identities.description: Written by build-report.mjs: { "<DQ-id>": "<identity>" }, what keeps finding ids stable across builds.

target.description: Optional. Where the app under test runs. kind: "local" for localhost, 127.x.x.x, [::1], *.localhost and file: URLs, "remote" for any other meta.app.url (a deployed build); validate.mjs derives it from meta.app.url and rejects a mismatch. localCommit: the commit of the checkout the agent read source from; deployedCommit: the commit the target runs (default meta.app.commit). On a remote target findings are grounded in the capture (open findings need app-side evidence) and a meta.degradations entry is expected when the local commit is unknown or differs.

notChecked.description: Design-system checks that did not run, each with why: tokens, components (build-report.mjs: the audit skipped, or no component library configured). scorecard.designSystem shows such a check as null, never 0.

dsAudit.description: Optional summary of the design-system audit (scripts/ds-audit.mjs or by hand): elements checked, values that match no token, components that are not from the design system, and the audit's output file. Record how it ran in meta.tools.dsAudit.

How the design-system audit ran: script (scripts/ds-audit.mjs), manual (element by element, by hand) or none. Missing or none with open findings and no token or component finding is a validate.mjs warning: token and component mismatches were not looked for.

parity.errorMessage: scorecard.parity was removed: match and settled replace it (render-report.mjs --recompute drops it)

match.description: How much of the compared pages matches the design: the mean of matchByState; null when no state was measured. At most 99 while a divergence is open, at least 1 unless every state is 0. The headline number; the verdict still carries the severity.

matchByState.description: Per compared state and per MISSING_IN_CODE state: 100 minus the share of the page that differs (the larger of differences.<state>.differing and the pixel diff's percent) and is not settled: a region counts as settled only when every finding naming it is a settled divergence or a rejection a computed hint supports names it (differences.<state>.regions). 0 for a MISSING_IN_CODE state or a sameAs state with an open state finding.

settled.description: BLOCKER, WARNING and DS_CANDIDATE findings that are not dismissed (total), and how many of them are not open (count): "count of total findings settled".

verdict.description: INCOMPLETE: nothing was captured and compared (an empty state matrix, or no row PASS, FAIL or MISSING_IN_CODE). It is not a result: fix the capture and run the pass again.

percent.description: Differing pixels as a percent of the compared area (the pixels both images have).

designHeight.description: Height in pixels of the design image diff.mjs compared (before padding).

appHeight.description: Height in pixels of the app image diff.mjs compared (before padding).

designWidth.description: Width in pixels of the design image diff.mjs compared (before padding).

appWidth.description: Width in pixels of the app image diff.mjs compared (before padding).

paddedRight.description: diff.mjs padded the narrower image on the right to the wider one's width; the padded columns are not compared (paddedRegions). side: the image that was narrower; cols: how many columns were added.

padded.description: diff.mjs padded the shorter image to the taller one's height; the padded rows are not compared (paddedRegions). side: the image that was shorter; rows: how many rows were added.

paddedRegions.description: diff.mjs: the parts only one image has, not compared (x, y, w, h, unmasked pixels, side = the smaller image, sizeDiff { axis, px }). Unmasked pixels raise the band to review and add a REVIEW reason naming the size difference; they never count in percent or match.

masks.description: diff.mjs: the masked rectangles (not compared) and the pixels each covers.

verified.description: PASS or FAIL rows that were compared (a pixel diff against a design image; captured.comparison), not only captured.

partial.description: Optional: verified rows captured only in part.

unexplained.description: Findings with resolution FIX_CODE or UNCLASSIFIED that are not ticketed debt.

debt.description: Triage items decided "debt", and how many of them have a ticket.

loopClosed.description: unexplained is 0, there are no open decisions and the verdict is not INCOMPLETE.

designSystem.description: Open findings by design-system kind: tokens = ledger style whose expected.token is set and differs from actual.token; components = ledger component; motion = ledger motion. tokens or components is null when that check did not run and nothing was found (meta.notChecked or no design-system audit): not checked, never 0.

rejected.description: Present when report.rejections is: how many worklist, audit and compare rejections, and pageShare = the largest rejected worklist share (percent) of any one state's page.

unpinned.description: Optional (render-report.mjs --recompute writes it): open FIX_CODE findings without a pin (no evidence entry with both state and crop), each exempt or carrying unpinnedReason.

backfill.description: Design backfill (step 2), present only when report.backfill is set: candidates = items; toBuild = decision build without a Figma frame yet; built = items with figma set; notNeeded; pending; ready = loopClosed or backfill.gate.override is set. Never changes match, verdict, unexplained, loopClosed or designSystem.

triage.description: The person's fix-now / debt decision for every triageable finding (FIX_CODE with severity BLOCKER, WARNING or DS_CANDIDATE), each exactly once. A BLOCKER can never be debt; DISMISSED and INTENTIONAL findings never appear.

ticketsAuthorized.description: Optional. Recorded by apply-decisions.mjs from the decisions document's "tickets": true when the reviewer authorised creating tickets for the debt items, false when they did not. Absent when the triage did not come from a decisions document.

state.description: Normalised state id: with-data, empty, loading, error, hover, focus, active, selected, disabled, … Multi-screen passes write "<screen>/<state>" (e.g. "cart/empty").

screen.description: Multi-screen passes: the meta.screens id this state belongs to (the prefix of state).

frame.description: Optional: the designed frame's full size. validate.mjs checks the compared design image is not shorter (a truncated comparison).

captured.description: Images of this state: design (exported from Figma or captured from the prototype), app and diff.

page.description: What the app capture of this state covered, from capture.json: width and height = the page's full scroll size in CSS px (capture.json page), image = the PNG size (capture.json size), fullPage = the whole scroll size was captured, clipped = how many scroll containers still hide content in the screenshot (capture.json clipped.length). validate.mjs checks the app image is not smaller than the page.

partial.description: true: the state was captured only in part on purpose (meta.degradations has step "capture-coverage:<state>"). It counts as verified only in part and holds the verdict at REVIEW.

viewportOnly.description: true: a deliberate first-screen capture (fullPage false: an overlay, a modal) whose image covers the state's design frame; the whole-page check accepts it.

sameAs.description: The state this one was captured identical to (capture.json sameAs: its driver changed nothing on the page). build-report.mjs requires an open state finding or a MISSING_IN_CODE override for it.

comparison.description: How the state was compared with the design (build-report.mjs writes it): pixelDiff = a pixel diff ran; worklist = the page was walked region by region; compareRows = compare.json rows of the state. A PASS or FAIL row needs pixelDiff true or compareRows above 0: a worklist alone is not a comparison.

figma.errorMessage: captured.figma was renamed to captured.design in 2.0

x-removed.MISSING_IN_DESIGN: MISSING_IN_DESIGN was removed in 2.0: the state matrix lists only states the design defines; drop this row

screen.description: Multi-screen passes: the meta.screens id of the finding.

rank.description: Derived by render-report.mjs when null. fix-now/debt: FIX_CODE findings with severity BLOCKER, WARNING or DS_CANDIDATE (the first topN by score are fix-now); none: everything else.

x-removed.sync-figma: the sync-figma bucket was removed in 2.0: FIX_CODE findings are fix-now or debt, everything else none

signoff.description: Required when resolution is INTENTIONAL, unless knownDrift cites a known drift (scripts/validate.mjs enforces it). by and reason are never blank.

by.errorMessage: must name who signed off (not blank)

date.errorMessage: must be a date (2026-01-31) or an ISO-8601 date-time (2026-01-31T12:00:00Z)

reason.errorMessage: must say why the divergence is accepted (not blank)

previousResolution.description: The resolution before this sign-off or dismissal, restored by an undo (dismiss.mjs --undo). Absent means FIX_CODE.

enteredBy.description: Set by build-report.mjs on a sign-off that came through findings.json: nobody confirmed it, so the finding stays open until a person accepts it in the review. Sign-offs from the review or a known drift's "Signed off" line have none.

dismissal.description: Required when resolution is DISMISSED. not-an-issue: the difference is not real or does not matter; remove: out of this QA (duplicate, out of scope, not this team's surface).

priorRef.description: id of the dismissed-log entry when re-applied from an earlier pass

previousResolution.description: The resolution before this sign-off or dismissal, restored by an undo (dismiss.mjs --undo). Absent means FIX_CODE.

knownDrift.description: The known-drift id (e.g. "KD-3") an INTENTIONAL finding cites.

dataReason.description: Required for resolution DATA (an evidence gate): at least 20 characters saying which data differs and why it is not a code problem.

unpinnedReason.description: Why an open FIX_CODE finding has no pin (no evidence entry with both state and crop): at least 20 characters naming what is absent from every capture. Not needed when the finding's state is MISSING_IN_CODE and has no app capture. Ignored (a warning) when the finding has a pin.

resolution.errorMessage: must be NONE when severity is PASS or CANNOT_VERIFY
must not be NONE when severity is BLOCKER, WARNING or DS_CANDIDATE (use FIX_CODE, INTENTIONAL, DATA, DISMISSED or UNCLASSIFIED)

bucket.errorMessage: must be "fix-now" or "debt" for a FIX_CODE finding with severity BLOCKER, WARNING or DS_CANDIDATE
must be "none": only FIX_CODE findings with severity BLOCKER, WARNING or DS_CANDIDATE are ranked

property.description: What animates: opacity, transform, height, background-color, … or "animation".

observed.description: null: nothing animates in the app (missing motion).

hidden.description: What capture.mjs hid or removed before the screenshot (preCapture): not compared.

figma.errorMessage: evidence.states.<state>.figma was renamed to design in 2.0

type.description: transition, animation, smart-animate, dissolve, move-in, slide, push, none, …

motionSpec.description: Shape of ledgers.motion[].expected / observed (type is checked where it is used: observed may be null).

backfill.description: Design backfill (step 2 of 2): states the app has but the design does not, to be built back into Figma with the design-system library once production matches the design (step 1). Never part of stateMatrix, findings, parity, verdict, unexplained, loopClosed, triage or designSystem. Validator: item ids unique; screen rules as for findings; not-needed needs a reason; figma only with decision build; a figma frame while not ready (no loopClosed, no override) is a warning (backfill.mjs --record refuses it; a later pass that reopens step 1 keeps frames built earlier); no item shares a state id with a stateMatrix row.

override.description: Building before step 1 is closed (scorecard.loopClosed false) needs a person's override with a reason.

state.description: Undesigned state id; multi-screen passes write "<screen>/<state>". Never a stateMatrix state.

screen.description: Multi-screen passes: the meta.screens id of the item.

detail.description: Where it was found, e.g. "OrdersTable.tsx:88 renders BulkBar when selection.length > 0".

driver.description: A capture.mjs DRIVER that puts the app into this state, or null.

captured.description: App-only evidence from capture.mjs --out <dir>/evidence/backfill (paths relative to report.json).

anchor.description: The designed frame the new frame sits next to.

figma.description: The frame built in Figma (decision build only).

roundTrip.description: Pixel diff of the 1x frame export against the app capture.

dsGaps.description: Components, variants or tokens the library lacks (design-system candidates of step 2, never step-1 findings).
